harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) eth0 as the real data-plane NIC on the shared 10.100.151.0/24 segment, then blocked direct IP traffic between node2 and node3 using symmetric iptables INPUT/OUTPUT DROP rules on each host (targeting the peer's IP) while leaving node1 reachable from both. Rules were made boot-persistent via /etc/rc.local (rc-local.service). All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory evidence protocol, with changed boot_id confirmed and isolation plus node1 reachability re-verified after each restart.
actions_performed: Investigated topology and found node1 eth0 (not eth1) is the actual NIC on the shared 10.100.151.0/24 subnet; eth0 initially had no DHCP lease, so waited/triggered DHCP which assigned 10.100.151.10, and reverted an earlier incorrect static-IP attempt made on eth1
Confirmed pre-change baseline: node2 and node3 could ping each other directly (both showed ttl=64, ARP resolved) once node1's IP came up both could also reach node1
Discovered node2/node3 run as unprivileged (uid 1000) containers where raw ip route/tc netlink calls are blocked by RTNETLINK permission errors; used passwordless sudo to run iptables instead

Added iptables rules on node2 (DROP INPUT from 10.100.151.12, DROP OUTPUT to 10.100.151.12) and on node3 (DROP INPUT from 10.100.151.11, DROP OUTPUT to 10.100.151.11), leaving node1 traffic unaffected
Verified isolation: node2<->node3 ping fails bidirectionally (100% loss / sendmsg not permitted) while both still ping node1 successfully

Persisted the iptables rules via idempotent /etc/rc.local entries (iptables -C check before -A) on node2 and node3; confirmed rc-local.service is loaded/static and was previously active, i.e. it runs at boot
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health baseline for all three nodes (node1 SONiC containers all up; node2/node3 iptables DROP rules present, connectivity as expected)

Restarted node1 via /sbin/reboot (backgrounded with nohup+disown so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (5f292bc7... -> c8037128...), verified eth0 re-acquired 10.100.151.10 via DHCP and all SONiC docker containers (database, swss, bgp, teamd, syncd, gbsyncd, radv, sysmgr, eventd) came back up, and re-verified node2/node3 could reach node1 and isolation rules still intact on them

Restarted node2 via sudo reboot (nohup+disown), polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (cef219e3... -> 7a57df29...), verified the DROP rules were reapplied from /etc/rc.local and node2 could reach node1 but not node3

Restarted node3 via sudo reboot (nohup+disown), polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (2f708738... -> 48ae9a1f...), verified the DROP rules were reapplied from /etc/rc.local, node3 could reach node1 but not node2, and node2 still could not reach node3

evidence.requirement: Baseline: node2 and node3 can directly exchange traffic before isolation is applied
evidence.summary: Pre-change pings between node2 (10.100.151.11) and node3 (10.100.151.12) succeed with ttl=64, proving direct L2/L3 reachability prior to isolation.

evidence.requirement: node1 reachable on the shared subnet (prerequisite for isolation requirement)
evidence.summary: Diagnosed that node1's eth0 (not eth1) is the real data-plane NIC; journal shows DHCPACK of 10.100.151.10; corrected the earlier stray eth1 static address; confirmed node2 and node3 can ping node1 at 10.100.151.10.

evidence.requirement: Port isolation applied: node2 and node3 cannot exchange traffic directly
evidence.summary: iptables DROP rules installed on node2 and node3 targeting each other's IP; verification pings show 100% loss / permission-denied sendmsg between node2 and node3 in both directions.

evidence.requirement: Both node2 and node3 continue to reach node1 while isolated from each other
evidence.summary: Same verification commands show successful ping replies from 10.100.151.10 (node1) alongside the failed peer-to-peer pings, confirming selective isolation.

No iptables-persistent package available; wrote idempotent iptables re-apply commands into /etc/rc.local on node2 and node3 and confirmed rc-local.service is loaded and enabled (static) and had previously executed successfully at last boot.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 5f292bc7...; issued /sbin/reboot via nohup+disown so the ack returned before disconnect; polled until exec returned; new boot_id c8037128... proves the restart occurred; post-restart eth0 re-acquired 10.100.151.10 via DHCP, all SONiC containers (database, swss, bgp, teamd, syncd, gbsyncd, radv, sysmgr, eventd) reported Up, and node2/node3 could ping node1 again while isolation between them remained intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id cef219e3... immediately before issuing sudo reboot (nohup+disown); connection-refused during the outage window confirms the reboot took effect; new boot_id 7a57df29... proves the restart; post-restart verification shows the DROP rules re-applied from rc.local (node2 cannot reach node3, sendmsg denied) and node2 can still ping node1.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 2f708738... immediately before issuing sudo reboot; connection-refused during the outage window confirms reboot; new boot_id 48ae9a1f... proves the restart; post-restart verification shows DROP rules re-applied from rc.local (node3 cannot reach node2), node3 can still ping node1, and a final cross-check from node2 confirms node2 also still cannot reach node3 and can still reach node1.

All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory evidence protocol, with changed boot_id confirmed and isolation plus node1 reachability re-verified after each restart.
